==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|annullen}}, from {{der|en|fro|anuller}}, from {{der|en|la|annullō||annihilate, annul}}, from {{com|la|ad|t1=to|nūllus|t2=none, not any|nocat=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{rhymes|en|ʌl|s=2}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈnʌl/|a=RP,GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-annul.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈnɐl/|a=AU,NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/əˈnʊl/|a=Northern England}}
* {{homophones|en|Anal}} {{qualifier|an ethnic group in India; not to be confused with ''[[anal]]'', which is not homophonous}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|++}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To formally [[revoke]] the validity of.
#: {{ant|en|uphold}}
#* {{RQ:William James Varieties|chapter=Lecture 2|passage=If you ask how religion thus falls on the thorns and faces death, and in the very act '''annuls''' annihilation, I cannot explain the matter, for it is religion's secret, and to understand it you must yourself have been a religious man of the extremer type.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To dissolve (a [[marital]] union) on the grounds that it is not valid.
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cancel out]].
#: {{ux|en|They tried to reassure me but I was not able to '''annul''' my fears.}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|annullability|annullable|annuller|annullity|annulment|disannul}}

====Related terms====

* {{s|dissolve (a marital union)}} {{l|en|dissolve}}
